text: Review: 'Caravans of Silk and Silver' by Tomas Reyna. Reyna's new history of the Silk Road sets out to correct the image of a single highway between China and Rome. Drawing on customs records, merchant letters and recent archaeology, he shows instead a shifting web of regional routes on which few traders ever travelled from end to end. The strongest chapters cover the Sogdian merchants of Central Asia and the role of oasis cities such as Samarkand. The book sometimes drowns in detail, and the maps are too small, but it is the most readable one-volume account I know. Recommended for anyone who enjoys popular histories of the medieval world.

A five-year survey of reefs off the Velan Islands found that 62% of hard coral colonies bleached during last summer's marine heatwave, the worst event since monitoring began. Divers from the Velan Marine Institute photographed the same 40 transects each year, recording colour, mortality and the arrival of new coral recruits. Branching species such as staghorn coral suffered most, while massive boulder corals largely recovered within six months. The team links the bleaching to sea surface temperatures that stayed 1.5 °C above the seasonal average for nine weeks, and recommends protecting cooler, deeper reefs that may act as refuges for coral larvae.

Bathroom renovation, update three. The old tub surround is gone, and the walls are now cement board with a liquid waterproofing membrane painted over every seam and screw head, two coats, running up to the ceiling in the shower area. This weekend I'm tiling: 30 by 60 cm porcelain in a third-offset pattern, which should avoid the lippage you get when long tiles are centred on each other. I bought a levelling clip system after reading too many horror stories. The grout will be a light grey epoxy, which is harder to work with than cement grout but won't stain. Still deciding whether to replace the extractor fan while the ceiling is open.

How long did it take to build a medieval castle? Surviving building accounts from the thirteenth century suggest that a large stone castle usually took somewhere between five and fifteen years, and the work came in seasons. Masons laid stone from spring to autumn, then covered the tops of unfinished walls with straw or turf to protect the mortar from winter frost. Most of the workforce were not masons at all but diggers, carters and quarrymen, often summoned from distant counties by royal order. Lords who could not wait for stone often threw up a motte-and-bailey castle of earth and timber first, and replaced it with a stone keep decades later.

The Mediterranean diet is a dietary concept that was first proposed in 1975 by American biologist Ancel Keys and chemist Margaret Keys. It is inspired by the eating habits and traditional foods of Greece, Italy and the Mediterranean coasts of France and Spain, as observed in the late 1950s to early 1960s. It is distinct from both Mediterranean cuisine, which encompasses the diverse culinary traditions of Mediterranean countries, and from the Atlantic diet of northwestern Spain and Portugal, albeit with some shared characteristics. The Mediterranean diet is the most well-known and researched dietary pattern in the world.

Advice needed for my first ball python. Mochi is a four-month-old female, about 40 cm long, living in a 120 by 60 cm PVC enclosure. The warm side sits at 31 °C over a thermostat-controlled heat mat and the cool side at about 25 °C, but the humidity keeps dropping to 45% overnight, and her last shed came off in patches. I've switched to coconut husk substrate and added a humid hide with damp moss. She took a frozen-thawed mouse last week but refused one yesterday. Is refusing food normal before a shed, and how high should the humidity be for a python her age?

Patch 1.14 for Ember Hollow. Balance: the Warden's shield bash cooldown increases from 8 to 11 seconds, because its stun was dominating ranked matches. Fire staffs now deal 10% less damage to bosses but make burn last a full second longer. Gameplay: players who disconnect during a co-op raid can now rejoin within three minutes without forfeiting their loot. The new Ashen Crossing map enters the ranked rotation. Fixes: resolved a bug where the Chapter 6 final boss could become stuck in the arena wall, and cut load times on consoles by about 15%. Season 4 begins next Thursday with a new battle pass.

Composer Ines Calloway spent last week at a scoring stage recording the soundtrack for 'The Lantern Keepers', the animated feature due in cinemas next spring. Working with a 70-piece orchestra and a children's choir, Calloway built the score around a single four-note motif that changes key each time the lighthouse appears on screen. Director Paul Annick said the music was written against a near-final edit so that each cue could be timed to individual frames. The soundtrack album will be released alongside the film, and two of its themes will be performed live with the orchestra at a concert screening in the autumn.

Red wine braised short ribs. This is the dish I make when the first cold weekend arrives. Season four pounds of bone-in short ribs generously and sear them hard in a Dutch oven until every side is deeply browned; don't rush this, because it is where the flavour comes from. Lift out the meat, soften onion, carrot and celery in the fat, stir in tomato paste, then deglaze with a bottle of dry red wine and reduce it by half. Return the ribs with beef stock, thyme and bay leaves, cover, and braise at 150 °C for three hours. My dog, Biscuit, supervised the whole afternoon from the kitchen doorway. Skim the fat, reduce the sauce, and serve over creamy polenta.

Ashby Rovers 2, Millbrook Town 1. Rovers came from behind to keep their promotion hopes alive at a rain-soaked Kestrel Park on Saturday. Millbrook went ahead after 23 minutes when Leo Varga headed in a corner at the near post, and they should have doubled the lead before half-time. The Rovers manager switched to a back three at the break and the change paid off: substitute Tomasz Weir equalised with a low shot on 61 minutes, and captain Jordan Fenn won it in stoppage time from the penalty spot after a handball. Rovers are now two points off the playoff places with four league games remaining.

PostgreSQL (  POHST-gres-kew-EL), also known as Postgres, is a free and open-source relational database management system (RDBMS) emphasizing extensibility and SQL compliance. PostgreSQL features transactions with atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability (ACID) properties, automatically updatable views, materialized views, triggers, foreign keys, and stored procedures.
It is supported on all major operating systems, including Windows, Linux, macOS,  FreeBSD,  OpenBSD and NetBSD, and handles a range of workloads from single machines to data warehouses, data lakes, or web services with many concurrent users.

Rust bubbling on the rear wheel arch of my 2009 estate car: worth fixing myself? The paint has blistered in a strip about 10 cm long along the lip of the arch, and when I pressed it a flake of metal came away, so I think it has rusted from the inside out where mud collects. The car is otherwise solid and passed its last inspection. My plan is to sand back to bare metal, treat it with a rust converter, fill any pinholes, then apply primer, colour-matched paint and lacquer. If there's an actual hole, is a fibreglass patch acceptable, or does it need a welded repair panel to pass the next roadworthiness test?

Dog training is a type of animal training, the application of behavior analysis which uses the environmental events of antecedents (trigger for a behavior) and consequences to modify the dog behavior, either for it to assist in specific activities or undertake particular tasks, or for it to participate effectively in contemporary domestic life. While training dogs for specific roles dates back to Roman times at least, the training of dogs to be compatible household pets developed with suburbanization in the 1950s.
A dog learns from interactions it has with its environment. This can be through classical conditioning, where it forms an association between two stimuli; non-associative learning, where its behavior is modified through habituation or sensitisation; and operant conditioning, where it forms an association between an antecedent and its consequence.

An electric vehicle (EV) is a vehicle propelled mostly by electric power. EVs encompass electric cars and other electric road vehicles (buses, trucks and personal transporters) as well as other types of land vehicles, such as electric rail vehicles (trains, trams and monorails). It also includes electric watercraft (boats and submersibles), aircraft (fixed-wing and multirotors), and spacecraft.
EVs originated in the late 19th century. Electricity was among the preferred methods for powering early motor vehicles because it was quieter, provided comfort, and ease of operation. However, its limited range hindered mass adoption throughout the 20th century. Internal combustion engines were the dominant propulsion mechanisms for cars and trucks for about 100 years, although electricity-powered locomotion became commonplace in other vehicle types, such as overhead line-powered mass transit vehicles, as well as special purpose vehicles such as mobility scooters.

Subject: Hollin Logistics, breach of contract. Hi Dana, following up on our call. Under section 7 of the master services agreement, Hollin committed to 98% on-time delivery, measured monthly. They have missed that for three consecutive months (91%, 89% and 93%), which triggers the cure period in clause 7.4: we must give written notice, and they then have 30 days to remedy before we can terminate for cause. Their account manager is now arguing that the indemnification clause caps any damages at one month's fees. Before we send the notice, can legal confirm whether our lost sales count as consequential damages excluded under section 11? I'd like to keep termination as leverage while we negotiate a service credit. Owen, Procurement

Stuttering in open-world games since my graphics card upgrade. I moved from an 8 GB card to a 16 GB one, and average frame rates went up as expected, but I now get hitches every few seconds when driving through the city in a racing game. Frame-time graphs show spikes to 80 ms. Things I've tried: a clean driver install, turning off the overlay, capping the frame rate at 90 FPS, and moving the game to my NVMe drive. CPU usage sits at around 70% on one core during the stutters. Is this shader compilation, a CPU bottleneck, or is my PCIe slot running at reduced speed? The motherboard is a few years old but has the latest BIOS.

Review: 'Ninth Round Light'. On paper this is just another boxing movie: a fading middleweight, one last title fight, a gym full of second chances. What lifts it is director Nadia Brennan's restraint. She shoots almost everything in long, unbroken takes, so that even the training montage plays as a single uncut minute of exhausted breathing. Rafe Okonkwo, in the lead, is remarkable in the quiet scenes with his estranged daughter, and the screenplay never pretends the climactic bout will fix things between them. The cinematography makes the ring look small and airless. At 2 hours 20 minutes it is overlong, but it is the best drama in cinemas this month. Four stars.

Physio session summary, week six after arthroscopic knee surgery. Range of motion is now 0 to 125 degrees and swelling is minimal. The patient can complete bodyweight squats to parallel without pain and hold a single-leg balance for 30 seconds. Plan for weeks seven to nine: introduce goblet squats and Romanian deadlifts at a light load, step-downs from a 20 cm box, and 20 minutes of stationary cycling on non-gym days. No running or jumping until quadriceps strength on the operated side reaches 80% of the other leg, which we will test at week ten. Ice after sessions if the swelling returns, and continue the home exercise sheet daily.

Maple Lane Studios has acquired the screen rights to Odessa Crane's 'Hollowmere' fantasy trilogy, the novels that spent much of last year on bestseller lists. The studio plans an eight-episode television series, with Crane co-writing the first two scripts, and has separately licensed the books to independent developer Lowtide Games for a narrative adventure game set a century before the first novel. Crane said she agreed to the deal because the series will follow the books' structure, one season per novel, rather than compressing the trilogy into a single film. Casting begins in the spring; the game is expected first, on PC and consoles, late next year.

Board memo: data breach notification obligations. On 2 October an attacker used a compromised contractor account to export the records of about 12,000 customers from our support platform, including names, email addresses and partial billing addresses. Outside counsel advises that under the data protection laws of two jurisdictions where we operate, we must notify the regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach and inform affected customers without undue delay. We filed both regulator notifications on 4 October. Remaining exposure: a possible fine, contractual notice duties to three enterprise clients, and reputational damage. Management recommends offering affected customers a year of credit monitoring and moving all contractors to hardware security keys.

2014 hatchback, about 142,000 km. For the last week there has been a metallic grinding from the front left wheel whenever I brake below about 30 km/h, and the steering wheel shudders slightly on harder stops. The brake pads were replaced 40,000 km ago. I took the wheel off, and the inner pad is almost down to the backing plate while the outer one still has plenty of material, so I suspect a sticking caliper slide pin. Is it safe to drive to the garage on Monday, and should I ask them to replace the rotors as well, given the shudder?

Our first morning in Hanoi began on a plastic stool on an Old Quarter pavement, with a bowl of pho bo that cost less than a coffee back home. The broth had simmered all night with charred onion, ginger, star anise and cinnamon, and the vendor added slices of rare beef that cooked in the bowl. Later we found bun cha, grilled pork patties with rice noodles and a sweet and sour dipping sauce, near Hoan Kiem Lake, and we finished the day with egg coffee in a narrow upstairs café. If you only have three days in the city, plan your sightseeing around meals rather than the other way round.

I left my agency job in March and now do freelance illustration full time. Income so far is about $46,000 from eleven clients, and I have just realised that nobody is withholding tax for me. An accountant friend says I should be paying quarterly estimated taxes and setting aside roughly 30% of every invoice. I'm also wondering whether to form an LLC or stay a sole proprietor, and whether I can deduct part of my rent for the home studio. At the moment everything runs through my personal checking account, which feels like a mess. What would you fix first: a separate business bank account, bookkeeping software, or a meeting with a tax professional?

Why are my session cookies not being sent? Our single-page app is served from app.example.com and calls an API on api.example.net. Since a browser update, users are logged out on every page refresh. The login response sets 'Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Path=/', but the cookie is missing from later requests. I think it's the SameSite default: with no attribute the browser treats the cookie as Lax, so it is never sent on cross-site fetches. Is the right fix 'SameSite=None; Secure', and does that weaken our CSRF protection enough that we need anti-CSRF tokens on every POST? Moving the API onto the same site isn't possible this quarter.

Our eight-year-old cat, Juniper, has started peeing on the bath mat instead of in her litter box. Nothing has changed at home except that we switched to a cheaper clumping litter about three weeks ago, and she still uses the box for everything else. The vet checked her last week and ruled out a urinary tract infection and bladder crystals, so we think it's behavioural. Is the new litter the likely cause? We have one box for one cat, in the laundry room next to the washing machine. Should we add a second box somewhere quieter, and how do we get the smell out of the mat so she doesn't keep going back to it?

Since my doctor told me to keep sodium under 1,500 mg a day for my blood pressure, I've been rebuilding my favourite recipes, and this lentil and vegetable soup is the one I make most. Sweat an onion, two carrots and two celery sticks in olive oil, add garlic, smoked paprika and cumin, then a cup of rinsed brown lentils and six cups of no-salt-added stock. Simmer for 35 minutes, stir in a handful of spinach, and finish with lemon juice and plenty of black pepper. The acid and spices do the work that salt used to do. Each of the six servings comes in at around 140 mg of sodium.

An individual retirement account (IRA) in the United States is a type of retirement savings plan offered by many financial institutions that provides tax advantages for retirement savings. It is a trust that holds investment assets purchased with a taxpayer's earned income for the taxpayer's eventual benefit in old age. An individual retirement account is a type of individual retirement arrangement as described in IRS Publication 590, Individual Retirement Arrangements (IRAs). Other arrangements include individual retirement annuities and employer-established benefit trusts.
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Individual retirement account", English Wikipedia

text: Compost is a mixture of ingredients used as plant fertilizer and to improve soil's physical, chemical, and biological properties. It is commonly prepared by decomposing plant and food waste, recycling organic materials, and manure. The resulting mixture is rich in plant nutrients and beneficial organisms, such as bacteria, protozoa, nematodes, and fungi. Compost improves soil fertility in gardens, landscaping, horticulture, urban agriculture, and organic farming, reducing dependency on commercial chemical fertilizers. The benefits of compost include providing nutrients to crops as fertilizer, acting as a soil conditioner, increasing the humus or humic acid contents of the soil, and introducing beneficial microbes that help to suppress pathogens in the soil and reduce soil-borne diseases.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) is a cryptographic protocol designed to provide secured communications over a computer network, such as the Internet. The protocol is widely used in applications such as email, instant messaging, and voice over IP, but its use in securing HTTPS remains the most publicly visible.
The TLS protocol aims primarily to provide security, including privacy (confidentiality), integrity, and authenticity through the use of cryptography, such as the use of certificates, between two or more communicating computer applications. It runs in the presentation layer and is itself composed of two layers: the TLS record and the TLS handshake protocols.
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Transport Layer Security", English Wikipedia

text: Build log, week two. The new editing workstation is finally assembled: a 16-core desktop CPU, 128 GB of DDR5 in four sticks, two NVMe drives in RAID 0 for scratch space, and a 1000 W power supply because I expect to add a second graphics card later. The first boot failed memory training until I dropped the RAM from its rated 6000 MT/s to 5200, which seems to be common with all four DIMM slots populated. Temperatures are fine under a 360 mm liquid cooler, peaking at 84 °C during a full render. Next step is updating the BIOS and checking whether the newer firmware lets the memory run at its rated speed.

Buying my first used car and trying not to get ripped off. I've narrowed it down to two compact SUVs at dealerships 20 minutes apart: a 2019 with 85,000 km listed at $17,900 and a 2021 with 52,000 km at $22,400. Both dealers keep steering the conversation towards monthly payments instead of the total price. My credit union has pre-approved me for a 48-month auto loan at 6.9%, so I'd rather negotiate the out-the-door price and bring my own financing. I've also booked a pre-purchase inspection with an independent mechanic for the 2021. Anything else I should check, such as dealer fees or extended warranties I should turn down?

Book club notes, October: 'The Salt Orchard' by Maren Holt. Eight of us came, and opinions split almost exactly in half. Everyone agreed that the first part, narrated by the eldest sister in the 1970s, is the strongest writing in the novel, especially the chapter about the flood. The jump to the granddaughter's present-day narrative divided us: half found the dual timeline clever, and half thought it flattened the ending. We spent a long time on whether the unreliable narrator was obvious from the start. Average rating 3.6 out of 5. Next month is the short story collection 'Small Hours'; Priya is hosting, so bring something for the potluck.

Bug report from QA: version 3.8.0 of the Fernwood Notes iOS app crashes immediately on launch for users upgrading from 3.7.x; fresh installs are fine. The crash log points at the Core Data migration. The new archivedAt attribute was added to the model without creating a new model version, so lightweight migration fails and we hit a fatalError while setting up the persistent container. Reproduced on the iPhone simulator by installing 3.7.4, creating a few notes, then installing the 3.8.0 build over it. Proposed fix: add a versioned data model, mark it current, and replace the fatalError with a recovery path. We should pause the phased App Store rollout until a patched build is approved.

How I cut our grocery bill by about a quarter without extreme couponing. First, I plan meals around the weekly flyers from the two supermarkets nearest us and build the shopping list from what's on sale. Second, I compare the unit price on the shelf tag rather than the package price, because the 'family size' box is often more expensive per 100 g. Third, I stack the store's digital coupons with manufacturer coupons, but only on things we would buy anyway. Finally, store brands for staples like flour, rice and tinned tomatoes. Our family of four went from roughly $1,100 a month to $820, and the difference now goes straight into savings.

On-call note, 02:10. Users reported intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors from the checkout API. The load balancer showed two of six targets flapping between healthy and unhealthy. Cause: Tuesday's deploy pushed the service's startup time to about 40 seconds, but the health check still allows only 30 seconds before marking a new container unhealthy, so the autoscaler kept replacing instances that never became ready. Mitigation: raised the health check grace period to 90 seconds and the unhealthy threshold from 2 to 3; the errors stopped by 02:35. Follow-up: add a separate readiness endpoint, and alert on target flapping rather than waiting for customer reports.

My lease ended on 31 August and I moved out after a professional clean, with dated photos of every room. Six weeks later the landlord still hasn't returned my $1,800 security deposit and won't answer emails. Our state's statute gives landlords 21 days to return the deposit or send an itemised list of deductions, and says wilful failure can mean double damages. I've drafted a demand letter that cites the statute and gives him ten days to pay. If he ignores it, is small claims court the right next step, and does the letter need to go by certified mail to count?

From 1 March, shops in the town of Wexley will no longer be allowed to hand out single-use plastic carrier bags, under an ordinance the council passed on Monday by seven votes to two. Retailers may offer paper or reusable bags for a minimum charge of 25 cents, with the money kept by the store. Businesses that break the rule face a warning and then fines of up to $500. Councillors cited litter in the Wexley River and the cost of clearing bags from storm drains. Shoppers are being encouraged to bring their own bags to the checkout, and the town will give away 5,000 reusable totes at the farmers' market.

The Legend of Zelda is a video game series created by Japanese game designers Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka. It is primarily developed and published by Nintendo, but some installments and re-releases have been outsourced to Flagship, Grezzo, and Tantalus Media. 
The series centers on the various incarnations of Link, a courageous young boy of the elf-like Hylian race, and Princess Zelda, a princess within the bloodline of the goddess Hylia. They fight to save the land of Hyrule from Ganon, an evil warlord turned demon king who wishes to use the Triforce, a sacred relic that can grant any wish its user desires when complete, to remake the world in his own dark image.
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "The Legend of Zelda", English Wikipedia

text: Dear Mr and Ms Adeyemi, thank you for coming to Thursday's conference. As we discussed, Kofi's reading fluency has improved this term (he now reads grade-level passages at about 95 words per minute), but his comprehension scores lag behind, particularly when a question asks him to infer a character's motives. In class we will be using guided reading groups twice a week, with short discussion questions. At home it would help if you read with him for fifteen minutes most evenings and asked him to predict what will happen next or explain why a character acted as they did. We will reassess in January. Best wishes, Ms Laurent, Year 3 (laurent@example.com)

Photosynthesis is a system of biological processes by which photopigment-bearing autotrophic organisms, such as most plants, algae and cyanobacteria, convert light energy—typically from sunlight—into the chemical energy necessary to fuel their metabolism. The term photosynthesis usually refers to oxygenic photosynthesis, a process that releases oxygen as a byproduct of water splitting. Photosynthetic organisms store the converted chemical energy within the bonds of intracellular organic compounds (complex compounds containing carbon), typically carbohydrates like sugars (mainly glucose, fructose and sucrose), starches, phytoglycogen and cellulose. When needing to use this stored energy, an organism's cells then metabolize the organic compounds through cellular respiration. Photosynthesis plays a critical role in producing and maintaining the oxygen content of the Earth's atmosphere, and it supplies most of the biological energy necessary for complex life on Earth.

Help: my tomatoes have dark, leathery patches on the bottom. This is my second year growing tomatoes in raised beds, and the first ripening fruits on the 'Roma' plants all have sunken black spots at the blossom end. The plants themselves look healthy. A neighbour says it's blossom end rot and a calcium problem, so should I be adding crushed eggshells or a calcium spray? We had a very dry fortnight followed by heavy rain, and I've been watering by hand whenever I remember. The beds were filled with bagged compost and topsoil last spring.

Jazz is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Its roots are in blues, ragtime, European harmony, African rhythmic rituals, spirituals, hymns, marches, vaudeville song, and dance music. Since the 1920s Jazz Age, it has been recognized as a major form of musical expression in both traditional and popular music. Jazz is characterized by swing and blue notes, complex chords, call and response vocals, polyrhythms and improvisation.

Pride and Prejudice is a novel by English author Jane Austen. Written when she was aged 20–21, it was her third novel written and became the second to see print when it was published in 1813. A novel of manners, it follows the character development of Elizabeth Bennet, the protagonist of the book, who learns about the repercussions of hasty judgments and comes to appreciate the difference between superficial goodness and actual goodness.
Her father, Mr Bennet—owner of the Longbourn estate in Hertfordshire—has five daughters; but this estate is entailed and so can only be inherited in the male line. To his regret, he has failed to save out of the income from the Longbourn estate to provide for his daughters. From the Bennets' perspective, it is imperative that at least one of their daughters marry well to support the others, which is a primary motivation driving the plot.
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Pride and Prejudice", English Wikipedia

text: ValueError when calling predict on my scikit-learn Pipeline. I built a Pipeline with a ColumnTransformer (OneHotEncoder on 'region' and 'plan', StandardScaler on the numeric columns) feeding a GradientBoostingClassifier that predicts customer churn. fit() works and cross-validation gives a ROC AUC of 0.81, but predict() on the new month's data raises 'Found unknown categories ['north-east'] in column 0 during transform'. I assumed the pipeline would cope with new values. Do I need handle_unknown='ignore' on the encoder, and is it safe to set that after the model has been trained, or do I have to refit the whole pipeline? A sample of the pandas DataFrame is below.

Type 2 diabetes (T2D), formerly known as adult-onset diabetes, is a form of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance, and relative lack of insulin. Common symptoms include increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue and unexplained weight loss. Other symptoms include increased hunger, having a sensation of pins and needles, and sores (wounds) that heal slowly. Symptoms often develop slowly. Long-term complications from high blood sugar include heart disease; stroke; diabetic retinopathy, which can result in blindness; kidney failure; and poor blood flow in the lower limbs, which may lead to amputations. A sudden onset of hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state may occur; however, ketoacidosis is uncommon.

After a third dry winter, the Arvale Valley water district will begin a cloud seeding trial in January. Aircraft will release silver iodide particles into passing winter storms, giving water vapour a surface to freeze onto so that more of it falls as snow over the upper watershed. The district hopes to raise the snowpack by 5 to 10%, enough to help refill the reservoir that supplies 80,000 residents and nearby farms. Scientists at the regional university will compare precipitation from seeded and unseeded storms over three seasons, since earlier studies have struggled to separate the effect of seeding from natural variation. Critics worry about silver accumulating in soils and streams.

A graphics processing unit (GPU) is a specialized electronic circuit designed for digital image processing and to accelerate computer graphics, being present either as a component on a discrete graphics card or embedded on motherboards, mobile phones, personal computers, workstations, and game consoles. GPUs are also increasingly being used for artificial intelligence (AI) processing and model training due to linear algebra acceleration, which is also used extensively in graphics processing.
Although there is no single definition of the term, and it may be used to describe any video display system, in modern use a GPU includes the ability to internally perform the calculations needed for various graphics tasks, like rotating and scaling 3D images, and often the additional ability to run custom programs known as shaders. This contrasts with earlier graphics controllers known as video display controllers which had no internal calculation capabilities, or blitters, which performed only basic memory movement operations. The modern GPU emerged during the 1990s, adding the ability to perform operations like drawing lines and text without CPU help, and later adding 3D functionality.
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Graphics processing unit", English Wikipedia

text: Ticket #4412: order history page timing out. Since we moved the storefront from the old monolith to the new Django service, the order history page takes 9 to 12 seconds for customers with long histories. The query log shows the view running one SELECT for the orders and then a separate SELECT for each order's line items, so a customer with 300 orders triggers more than 1,500 queries. Classic N+1. In a branch I added select_related for the customer join and prefetch_related for the line items, and locally the page dropped to about 40 queries. We should also add a composite index on (customer_id, created_at), because the default ordering sorts on created_at. Could someone from the database team review the migration before Thursday's deploy?

Support ticket from Calder Street Kitchen. During Friday's dinner rush, the ordering app on our servers' tablets kept showing 'Waiting for connection', and orders sat on the tablets instead of printing in the kitchen. It happened roughly every ten minutes, for about 30 seconds each time. The tablets connect to the restaurant Wi-Fi, and the kitchen printer and the router are on the same network, behind the bar. We added a second access point in the dining room last month. Nobody has changed the menu or the app settings. Could the two access points be on the same channel, or is the router dropping DHCP leases? We need this fixed before Saturday service.

The marathon is a long-distance foot race with a distance of 42.195 kilometres (c. 26.22 mi), usually run as a road race, but the distance can be covered on trail routes. The marathon can be completed by running or with a run/walk strategy. There are also wheelchair divisions. More than 800 marathons are held worldwide each year, with the vast majority of competitors being recreational athletes, as larger marathons can have tens of thousands of participants.
A creation of the French philologist Michel Bréal inspired by a story from Ancient Greece, the marathon was one of the original modern Olympic events in 1896 in Athens. The distance did not become standardized until 1921. The distance is also included in the World Athletics Championships, which began in 1983. It is the only running road race included in both championship competitions (walking races on roads are also contested in both).

The Montessori method of education is a type of educational method that encourages children's natural interests and activities rather than formal teaching methods. A Montessori classroom places an emphasis on hands-on learning and developing real-world skills, such as problem solving and helping and teaching each other. It emphasizes independence and it views children as naturally eager for knowledge and capable of initiating learning in a sufficiently supportive and well-prepared learning environment. It also discourages some conventional methods of measuring achievement, such as grades and tests.
The method was started in the 20th century by Italian physician Maria Montessori, who developed her theories through scientific experimentation with children in many different situations. The method has since been used in many parts of the world, in public and private schools.

A mobile app or application is a computer program or software application designed to run on a mobile device such as a smartphone, tablet, or smartwatch. Mobile applications often stand in contrast to desktop applications which are designed to run on desktop computers, and web applications which run in mobile web browsers rather than directly on the mobile device.
Apps were originally intended for productivity assistance such as email, calendar, and contact databases, but the public demand for apps caused rapid expansion into other areas such as mobile games, factory automation, GPS and location-based services, order-tracking, and ticket purchases, so that there are now millions of apps available. Many apps require Internet access. Apps are generally downloaded from app stores, which are a type of digital distribution platforms.

Strength training, also known as weight training or resistance training, is exercise designed to improve physical strength. It may involve lifting weights, bodyweight exercises (such as push-ups, pull-ups, and squats), isometrics (holding a position under tension, such as planks), and plyometrics (explosive movements like jump squats and box jumps).
Training works by progressively increasing the force output of the muscles and uses a variety of exercises and types of equipment. Strength training is primarily an anaerobic activity, although circuit training also is a form of aerobic exercise.
Strength training can increase muscle, tendon, and ligament strength as well as bone density, metabolism, and the lactate threshold; improve joint and cardiac function; and reduce the risk of injury in athletes and the elderly. For many sports and physical activities, strength training is central or is used as part of their training regimen.

Present-day climate change includes both global warming—the ongoing increase in global average temperature—and its wider effects on Earth's climate system. In a broader sense, climate change also includes previous long-term changes to Earth's climate. The modern-day rise in global temperatures is driven by human activities, especially fossil fuel (coal, oil and natural gas) burning since the Industrial Revolution. Fossil fuel use, deforestation, and some agricultural and industrial practices release greenhouse gases. These gases absorb some of the heat that the Earth radiates after it warms from sunlight, warming the lower atmosphere. Earth's atmosphere now has roughly 50% more carbon dioxide, the main gas driving global warming, than it did at the end of the pre-industrial era, reaching levels not seen for millions of years.

Black Friday is the Friday after Thanksgiving in the United States. It traditionally marks the start of the Christmas shopping season and is the busiest shopping day of the year in the United States. Many stores offer highly promoted sales at heavily discounted prices and often open early, sometimes as early as midnight or even on Thanksgiving. Some stores' sales continue to Monday ("Cyber Monday") or for a week ("Cyber Week").

CS 241, Introduction to Database Systems: course outline. This course covers the design and use of relational databases. Weeks 1 to 4: the relational model, SQL queries, joins and aggregation. Weeks 5 to 7: schema design, normalization to third normal form, and entity-relationship diagrams. Weeks 8 to 10: transactions, isolation levels and indexing. Assessment: weekly SQL problem sets (30%), a midterm exam (25%), a group project (30%) in which teams build a small web application in Python backed by PostgreSQL, and a final quiz (15%). Prerequisite: an introductory programming course. Office hours are on Tuesdays from 2 to 4 pm; send project questions to db-course@example.com.

Week four of my couch-to-5K plan, and I can finally run five minutes without stopping. The plan is three sessions a week: a five-minute brisk walk to warm up, then alternating intervals of running and walking, with the running portion growing a little each week until you can run for 30 minutes straight by week nine. Today was three minutes running and ninety seconds walking, repeated five times. My tip for anyone starting out: slow down. I was going far too fast in week one, and running at a pace where I can still talk has made the intervals feel doable. Rest days matter too; my shins stopped aching once I stopped running on consecutive days.

Notes from today's experiment review. We fine-tuned the small sentiment classifier on the 4,000 labelled support emails for ten epochs. Training loss kept falling, but validation loss bottomed out at epoch three and climbed afterwards, and validation accuracy dropped from 88% to 83%: textbook overfitting. Next run: keep the best checkpoint by validation loss (early stopping with a patience of two), add dropout of 0.1 to the classification head, and lower the learning rate from 5e-5 to 2e-5. Marta also suggested augmenting the minority 'angry' class, which is only 6% of the data and has the worst recall. Given the class imbalance we will compare macro-F1 rather than accuracy.

Homemade peanut butter and pumpkin dog treats. Our vet suggested cutting back on shop-bought treats for our beagle, who is a little heavy, so I started baking these. Whisk one egg with half a cup of plain pumpkin purée and a quarter cup of xylitol-free peanut butter; check the label, because xylitol is toxic to dogs. Stir in about two cups of oat flour until you have a stiff dough, roll it out to half a centimetre and cut small shapes. Bake at 160 °C for 25 minutes, then turn the oven off and leave them inside to dry out so they keep for two weeks. Each treat is around 15 calories.

Separating smart-home gadgets from the rest of my network. I have about fifteen cheap IoT devices (plugs, two cameras, a robot vacuum) and I don't trust their firmware. My plan is to put them on their own VLAN with a separate SSID, block all traffic from that VLAN to my main LAN with firewall rules, and only let them out to the internet. The router supports VLAN tagging and the mesh access points can broadcast several SSIDs. Two questions: do the cameras need mDNS reflection so the viewer can still discover them from the main network, and is it worth giving the IoT VLAN its own DHCP range and DNS resolver so I can log which servers they are calling home to?

StrideLog 5.2 release notes. New: heart-rate zone training. Pair a chest strap or watch and the app now shows which of five zones you are in during a run or ride, with a summary of time spent in each zone after the workout. New: recovery score. Each morning we combine last night's sleep duration, your resting heart rate and recent training load into a single score, and suggest an easy day when it drops. Improved: workout logging for strength sessions now supports supersets and rest timers. Fixed: GPS tracks no longer drop on Android phones when the screen locks. As always, your health data stays on your phone unless you turn on cloud backup.

A message to parents from the Riverside Youth Soccer League. From this season, every coach and referee must complete the online concussion awareness course before their first game. Any player who shows signs of a possible head injury, such as headache, dizziness, confusion, or being slow to get up after a collision, will be removed from play immediately and cannot return that day, even if they say they feel fine. Players must then bring written clearance from a doctor and complete a graded return-to-play programme lasting at least six days. We are also banning deliberate heading in matches for the under-10 age groups, following the national federation's guidance.

Astronomers at the Cerro Alto Observatory report detecting water vapour in the atmosphere of a planet orbiting a red dwarf 48 light-years away. The planet, about 1.6 times the size of Earth, passes in front of its star every 11 days. By measuring how starlight filters through the atmosphere during these transits, the team identified the absorption signature of water, along with hints of methane. The planet orbits near the inner edge of its star's habitable zone, although the researchers caution that frequent stellar flares may have stripped away much of its original atmosphere. Follow-up observations are planned for next year.

In deep learning, the transformer is a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism, in which input data such as text, images, or audio is  converted to a sequence of numerical representations called tokens, and each token is converted into a vector through an embedding layer. At each layer, each token is then contextualized within the scope of the context window with other (unmasked) tokens via a parallel multi-head attention mechanism, allowing the signal for key tokens to be amplified and less important tokens to be diminished. Because self-attention alone is permutation-invariant, transformers inject positional information, typically through positional encodings or learned positional embeddings, so token order can affect the output.

Three days on Java, from Yogyakarta to the volcanoes. We spent the first day around Yogyakarta, watching the sunrise from the upper terraces of Borobudur before the tour buses arrived. On day two a driver took us east across the island to Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park; we slept in a guesthouse on the crater rim and walked out at 3:30 am to watch the sun come up over the smoking cone of Mount Bromo. The final leg, to Ijen, meant another pre-dawn hike, this time with gas masks, to see the sulphur miners and the turquoise crater lake. Bring warm layers: the highlands are cold at night.

Visiting Pompeii in a day. Take the Circumvesuviana train from Naples to Pompei Scavi, a few minutes' walk from the main entrance, and arrive when the gates open: by noon the tour groups and the heat make the long straight streets hard going. Start at the Forum, where the outline of the city's temples and law courts is easiest to read, then walk to the House of the Faun and on to the amphitheatre at the far eastern end. It helps to remember what you are looking at: a Roman town of perhaps eleven thousand people, buried under volcanic ash when Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD and preserved almost exactly as it was. Bring water; there is little shade.

Six months into learning guitar, and barre chords are still beating me. F major at the first fret buzzes on the B and high E strings however hard I press, and my hand cramps after a minute. My teacher says pressing harder is the wrong instinct: roll the index finger slightly onto its bony edge, keep the thumb low behind the neck, and pull back with the arm instead of squeezing. She also suggested practising the shape at the fifth fret, where the string tension is lower, then sliding it down. Having the action lowered at a guitar shop helped more than I expected. Any other exercises that worked for you?

Incident summary: on Tuesday a developer committed a .env file containing a live payment-provider API key and our cloud storage access keys to a public repository. Automated secret scanning flagged the commit within four minutes. We revoked and rotated both keys within 25 minutes. The provider's logs show no use of the payment key, but the storage key was used twice from an unknown address to list buckets before it was revoked; no objects were downloaded. Actions: add .env to the template .gitignore, enforce a pre-commit secret-scanning hook, move all credentials into the secrets manager with short-lived tokens, and have CI pipelines fetch secrets at runtime instead of reading them from repository variables.

Runbook update: restoring the orders database. Our managed PostgreSQL instance now keeps automated daily snapshots for 14 days plus continuous write-ahead log archiving, which gives us point-in-time recovery to any second within that window. Last month's restore drill took 47 minutes for the 380 GB database, inside our one-hour recovery time objective. Procedure: create a new instance from the point-in-time restore, verify row counts against the replica, then switch the application's connection string and DNS record to the new endpoint. Never restore over the existing primary. A read replica in a second region is available for failover if the whole region goes down.

Harbour City FC has agreed a ten-year naming-rights deal with regional insurer Coastline Mutual, the club confirmed on Tuesday. The stadium will be renamed Coastline Mutual Park from next season under an agreement reported to be worth £3.5 million a year, the largest commercial deal in the club's history. Chief executive Helen Marsh said the income would fund a new training ground and help the club meet the league's spending rules without selling its best young players. Some supporters' groups criticised the loss of the ground's historic name, and the club has promised to keep 'The Wharf' on the main stand.

A copyright is a type of intellectual property that gives its owner the exclusive legal right to copy, distribute, adapt, display, and perform a creative work, usually for a limited time. The creative work may be in a literary, artistic, educational, or musical form. Copyright is intended to protect the original expression of an idea in the form of a creative work, but not the idea itself. A copyright is subject to limitations based on public interest considerations, such as the fair use doctrine in the United States and fair dealing doctrine in the United Kingdom.

Lesson plan, Year 7 music, week 5: rhythm and notation. Objective: students can read and clap simple rhythms using crotchets, quavers and minims, and write a four-bar rhythm of their own in 4/4 time. Starter (10 minutes): call-and-response clapping led by the teacher. Main activity (25 minutes): in pairs, students decode rhythm cards and perform them on untuned percussion, then compose a four-bar pattern and notate it on manuscript paper. Plenary (10 minutes): two pairs perform, and the class identifies the note values they hear. Differentiation: students who finish early add rests and a dotted rhythm. Homework: practise reading the rhythm sheet on the class website.

The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066 between the Norman-French army of William, Duke of Normandy, and an English army under the Anglo-Saxon King Harold Godwinson, beginning the Norman Conquest of England. It took place approximately 7 mi (11 km) northwest of Hastings, close to the present-day town of Battle, East Sussex, and was a decisive Norman victory.
The background to the battle was the death of the childless King Edward the Confessor in January 1066, which set up a succession struggle among several claimants to his throne.

text: Running a 3-billion-parameter language model inside a phone app is mostly a memory problem, not a compute problem. At 16-bit precision the weights alone need about 6 GB, more than most phones will give a single app. Quantizing to 4 bits cuts that to under 2 GB, and because generating each token reads every weight once, smaller weights also mean faster decoding: memory bandwidth, not the chip's peak throughput, sets the speed limit. In our tests the 4-bit build generated 18 tokens per second on a recent flagship phone, against 7 at 8 bits, with a small but measurable drop in answer quality on our evaluation set.

In commerce, supply chain management (SCM) deals with a system of procurement (purchasing raw materials/components), operations management, logistics and marketing channels, through which raw materials can be developed into finished products and delivered to their end customers. A more narrow definition of supply chain management is the "design, planning, execution, control, and monitoring of supply chain activities with the objective of creating net value, building a competitive infrastructure, leveraging worldwide logistics, synchronising supply with demand and measuring performance globally". This can include the movement and storage of raw materials, work-in-process inventory, finished goods, and end-to-end order fulfilment from the point of origin to the point of consumption. Interconnected, interrelated or interlinked networks, channels and node businesses combine in the provision of products and services required by end customers in a supply chain.

Kubernetes (), also known as K8s, is an open-source container orchestration system for automating software deployment, scaling, and management. Originally designed by Google, the project is now maintained by a worldwide community of contributors, and the trademark is held by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.
The name Kubernetes comes from the Ancient Greek term κυβερνήτης, kubernḗtēs (helmsman, pilot), which is also the origin of the words cybernetics and (through Latin) governor. "Kubernetes" is often abbreviated with the numerical contraction "K8s", meaning "the letter K, followed by 8 letters, followed by s".
Kubernetes assembles one or more computers, either virtual machines or bare metal, into a cluster which can run workloads in containers. It works with various container runtimes, such as containerd and CRI-O. Its suitability for running and managing workloads of all sizes and styles has led to its widespread adoption in clouds and data centers. There are multiple distributions of this platform—from independent software vendors (ISVs) as well as hosted-on-cloud offerings from all the major public cloud vendors.

Hi all, here's the plan for Lisbon. We land at 10:40 on Friday and the apartment in Alfama is ready from 2 pm, so we'll drop our bags at the luggage storage near Santa Apolónia station and find lunch. Saturday: tram 28 early, before the queues, then Castelo de São Jorge and sunset at the Miradouro da Senhora do Monte viewpoint. Sunday is the day trip to Sintra; trains leave Rossio every 20 minutes and take about 40, and we've booked Pena Palace for 11:00. Monday is free until the 18:15 flight home. Pick up a Viva Viagem card at the airport metro station and load it with credit; it covers the trams, buses and the Sintra train.

Citizen Kane is a 1941 American drama film directed, produced by, and starring Orson Welles and co-written by Welles and Herman J. Mankiewicz, and was Welles's first feature film. The quasi-biographical film examines the life and legacy of Charles Foster Kane, played by Welles, a composite character based on American media barons William Randolph Hearst and Joseph Pulitzer, and Chicago tycoons Samuel Insull and Harold McCormick, as well as aspects of the screenwriters' own lives.

Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that emphasizes code readability, simplicity, and ease-of-writing with the use of significant indentation, an extensive ("batteries-included") standard library, and garbage collection. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Guido van Rossum began working on Python in the late 1980s as a successor to the ABC programming language. Python 3.0, released in 2008, was a major revision and not completely backward-compatible with earlier versions. Beginning with Python 3.5, capabilities and keywords for typing were added to the language, allowing optional static typing.

I have a serious bug problem and I'm running out of ideas. Every new shoot on my climbing roses is coated in tiny green aphids, and the buds are starting to look distorted. I've been blasting them off with the hose every couple of days, which works for about 48 hours. I'd rather not spray anything that harms bees, since the roses grow next to my lavender bed. Would insecticidal soap be safe if I spray in the evening? I've also read about buying ladybird larvae. Has anyone had luck releasing them in a small backyard, or do they just fly off to the neighbours?
